description:
Team: Astro Squad | Project: Little Astronauts

We are 6 software developers creating an educational game that will encourage children to learn about NASA through interesting missions and quizzes.
summary: Little Astronauts is a browser game that trains kids aged 7–14 as junior astronauts. A robot friend living on Mars asks for help with missions driven by NASA data: clean the solar panels when dust rises, run to the shelter during solar flares reported by NASA DONKI, and keep warm on −78 °C nights. Kids then design their own Mars mission and keep a 4-person outpost alive for 30 sols, balancing life support, radiation shielding, power and food production, the same trade-offs that decide whether a real mission fails or succeeds. Talking-pet play (voice repeat, feeding, levels and gifts) keeps them coming back, and an AI voice helper explains hard missions in Bangla or English. It runs in any phone browser with no install.
details:
What it does

• Robot friend on Mars: kids talk to him (he repeats them in a robot voice), touch, feed and put him to sleep.

• Data-driven missions appear inside the game world, not as a list: read the weather station, clean dusty solar panels, close the habitat in a dust storm, shelter from solar flares, hold the heater on freezing nights, collect rock samples, dig for water ice, fly a small helicopter. Each mission ends with a real NASA fact.

• Missions give XP; every level unlocks a gift (7 emotes, 6 skins, 8 outfits).

• Learn mode: 21 levels of 3D lessons with quizzes (Earth, Sun, planets, Moon, rockets, astronauts, rovers, Mars, galaxies, black holes, exoplanets).

• Mission design: choose Gale or Jezero Crater, meet 4 crew roles, pack 20 cargo points (batteries, oxygen, water, food, spare parts, radiation shielding).

• 30-sol outpost: assign crew jobs and manage life support (oxygen, water), food production (greenhouse), power (solar and batteries), radiation (shielding and shelter mode), health and morale through dust storms, solar storms and breakdowns. Every job costs power, so kids feel the trade-offs that make a mission fail or succeed.

How it works

NASA data → Python processing → JSON → game engine. A Vercel function fetches live solar events from NASA DONKI every hour; another sends questions to Google Gemini. Firebase stores progress so the same game continues on phone and computer.

Benefits and intended impact

Kids learn by deciding, not by watching. It is free, works on low-cost phones, and supports Bangla and English, so children who never get to visit a science center can still train like junior astronauts. Our goal: every child, on any phone, learning to think like a mission engineer.

How it is creative

It mixes a talking-pet game kids already love with real Mars engineering. Missions are not a numbered list: they appear in the game world when NASA data says something is happening, like a dust storm or a solar flare.

Factors we considered

Child safety (short AI answers, no personal data asked, no ads), low-cost phones and slow internet (no install, no build step, works offline except AI and live data), two languages, voice input and read-aloud for kids who cannot read well yet, and honesty about data (live solar events vs. published rover ranges).

Tools

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, Web Speech API, Vercel serverless functions, Google Gemini API, Firebase Authentication and Firestore, Python.

Source code: https://github.com/Amzadullah/little-astronaut
